source.title: From Plato to Aristotle: Toward a General Theory of Representation Hypotheses
source.authors: Dai Shi; Andi Han; Xiao-Yu Li; Luke Thompson; José Miguel Hernández-Lobato

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices and experimental details, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests and refines representation-convergence claims. Its results show that measured alignment varies with the criterion, evaluation scale, preprocessing, layer protocol, and training objective; it also reports cases of incomplete alignment and failure of predicted convergence outside theoretical model assumptions.
record.gate_note: Rows below cover the study’s own measurements and experiments on pretrained models and controlled training. Cited findings from earlier studies and proposed future tests are not rows. The coupling-predictor test was not run because every candidate estimator failed its preliminary check; the paper reports this in the text but it is not a measured outcome of the predictor.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-modal size trends of mKNN and CKA on pretrained vision–language pairs from the PRH/ARH setup. It shows that the trends change with evaluation size, preprocessing, depth, layer aggregation and calibration, and it tests convergence across seeds and objectives in controlled training. Its argument is that existing convergence claims need restating as criterion-specific.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors argue that PRH, ARH, BPC and SOG conflict because they apply alignment criteria at different points of one lattice. ARH's loss of the CKA trend can come from calibrating a layer maximum, and calibrated fixed-depth CKA keeps its sign, so global convergence remains open. BPC's mKNN collapse is at least partly a scale (k/m) effect. SOG's MST overlap mostly repeats 1-NN overlap. For independently trained models, training procedure and objective decide which criteria are met reliably; this is proved in toy models, with several predictions failing in trained networks.
record.recipe_differences: Develops a lattice framework for comparing alignment criteria and tests scale, observable, preprocessing, and calibration effects rather than reproducing the original studies’ full methods. It also adds theoretical and controlled-training experiments on linear autoencoders, finite contrastive models, and CIFAR-5m networks.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome changes with evaluation-set size and k/m, similarity measure, feature preprocessing, layer depth, layer aggregation, calibration, model family, training objective, and training procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: On 136 pretrained vision–language pairs, scale and affine fits explain most of the squared-distance discrepancy (medians 0.681+0.190 at mid depth). A global monotone link adds only 0.0004–0.0012, leaving a residual of 0.10–0.12.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Differences between pretrained vision and language geometries beyond an affine map are residual noise rather than a monotone distortion.

fits_no_version.finding: MST overlap mostly repeats one-nearest-neighbor overlap: forest share of shared edges is 0.875/0.889, near the 0.85 random-subset expectation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spanning-tree overlap is not an independent measure of global structural convergence.

record.problems: Pretrained-model size trends are based on one draw of evaluation inputs and limited model families; exact trend p-values are weakly constrained by small numbers of model sizes in some families. Size, depth, width, and sometimes training data grow together. The estimated coupling predictor was not validated and its preregistered out-of-sample test was not run. Several controlled-network predictions failed outside theorem assumptions, and the authors note that their theorems do not establish the pretrained-model mechanisms.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the numerous individual COCO pair slopes and secondary elasticity analyses, the detailed per-family/per-layer baseline forecasts and pairwise calibration-order counts, and secondary network diagnostics. These are reported across Sections 5.2–5.6 and Appendices F.3–F.10; the retained rows prioritize results bearing directly on claim versions and distinct changes in outcome.

untested.parts: Capability or performance as the driver; scaling of the vision side (only language-model size varies, except a secondary last-layer analysis); independent variation of architectures and data across families.
Improvement of the vision models; capability measures rather than parameter count.
Recurrence of individual features or units across seeds in deep networks. Seed-pair results in CIFAR-5m networks and Pythia-410M exist in the text but are not rows.
Model stitching, relative representations, alignment without paired data, and linear-map loss between pretrained models.
Entire version: no measurement of recurring neurons, SAE features or circuits.
Out-of-distribution inputs and other datasets beyond WIT/COCO.
Plateau of alignment with scale; whether shared training data explains the pretrained-model trends.

missing.what: Linear AE with weight decay, tied weights or small init: neighbor-set, Gs and CKA agreement reliable for N≥2^12 (≥47/48, ≥488/500 at N=∞). SGD and Adam stay unreliable.

CIFAR-5m linear-head networks across seeds: trunk features reliable under every criterion at 250k in all arms but one cell. Head coordinates agree on neighbor sets 96/96 without weight decay but Gs only 65/96; weight decay gives 96/96.
Pythia-410M seed pairs: flat mKNN slope (median −0.01) vs −0.21 for vision pairs and −0.57 for vision–language pairs at k=10.
Layer-max mKNN and debiased CKA trends move ≤0.06 under calibration in all families: mKNN 1.00, 0.38, 1.00, 1.00 calibrated.
ARH pooled statistic on 187 pairs: CKA 0.50→0.40, mKNN 0.51→0.51. The difference of 0.10 has interval [−0.02, 0.24], so the ARH pattern is not established.
Vision-model size trend at the last layer: CKA minus permutation mean Tr=−0.04 vs mKNN 0.71 (p=0.005).
Plain ℓ2 layer-max calibration trends: LLaMA-1 −0.50→−0.56, OpenLLaMA −0.26→−0.62, Pythia 0.68→−0.06.
InfoNCE at temperatures 0.2 vs 0.5 in CIFAR-5m nets: 0/64 pairs agree on every criterion except the projector.

record.verdict_notes: Labels for V1/V2 rest mostly on BLOOMZ, with 3-size families (p≥1/6) for LLaMA-1 and OpenLLaMA. Size, depth and width are confounded, and results rest on one input draw. The reader's 'challenges V4' from r8/r9 was a misreading: those rows decompose discrepancy and do not measure mapping loss. The reader's 'challenges V7' from r25 had the direction reversed: cross-objective divergence supports V7's objective dependence. The Gibbs-model results are idealized minimizers, not trained networks. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Tests model-size trends in selected pretrained model families and criteria, but not whether capability or performance itself causes convergence, nor convergence across a broad sweep of independently varied architectures, objectives, data, and modalities.
Tests paired vision–language representations and some sentence encoders, but not a general sweep of model performance or all cross-modal pairings.
Tests neighbor agreement for seed pairs and shared projectors in linear autoencoders; it does not test recurrence of individual features across general neural networks.
Tests distance-map fits and monotone links in selected settings, but not stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
No experiment measures whether the same interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits recur across models.
Tests evaluation-set size, k/m, preprocessing, depth, calibration, and similarity criteria in the reported settings; it does not exhaust other datasets or all reasonable metrics.
Tests incomplete alignment and an objective-dependent mechanism in theoretical and controlled settings, but does not establish whether shared data or objectives explain the pretrained-model trends.
